title: Strategy Under Uncertainty
briefing: The board is setting the next five-year strategy. The strategy team has one forecast. The chair asks you to make sure the board decides with its eyes open.

context.text: Your emerging-risk signposts give the scenarios a ready-made set of indicators.
The liquidity buffer you set gives the board room to take strategic risk.

evidence.title: Strategy team forecast
evidence.body: Revenue doubles in five years: pharma 35%, electric fleet by 2030, two acquisitions.

evidence.title: Key uncertainties
evidence.body: Speed of pharma supplier consolidation; electric truck cost and range; regulation of refrigerants; availability of drivers and engineers; climate impacts on cold-chain demand.

evidence.title: Board dynamics
evidence.body: Two directors are strongly committed to the forecast; one is openly sceptical. The CEO wants approval in one meeting.

questions.prompt: Which scenario approach do you use?

options.label: Four scenarios built from the two most uncertain, most impactful drivers (pharma consolidation speed x electric fleet economics), each with signposts
The forecast plus and minus 10%
options.feedback: Sensitivity, not scenarios: same world, different numbers.

options.label: One worst case
options.feedback: Useful for resilience, not for strategy choices.

questions.prompt: What should the board look for in the strategy?

options.label: No-regret moves that work in every scenario, options to scale up when signposts confirm, and limits on irreversible bets
The plan that does best in the most likely scenario
options.feedback: Optimises for one future and breaks in others.

questions.prompt: How do you work with the committed directors and the CEO's one-meeting goal?

options.label: Walk the committed directors and the sceptic through the scenarios individually beforehand, and propose two sessions: explore, then decide
options.feedback: No surprises, and space for real challenge before commitment.

options.label: Present everything in the meeting
options.feedback: Committed directors defend positions in public.

options.label: Brief only the sceptic to strengthen the challenge

questions.prompt: How should the strategy connect to risk appetite?

options.label: Test each strategic move against the appetite statement and propose appetite changes explicitly where the strategy needs them
options.feedback: Strategy and appetite set together, not separately.

options.label: Update appetite after the strategy is approved
options.feedback: Then appetite just ratifies whatever was decided.

options.label: Keep them separate: appetite is about controls
options.feedback: Appetite is about how much risk to take in pursuit of objectives.

questions.prompt: Your closing line to the board:

options.label: "Under all four scenarios these three moves pay off; these two only pay if pharma consolidates fast, so we fund them in stages and watch these signposts."
"The forecast is achievable."
options.feedback: Not your role, and not what you found.

options.label: "The future is too uncertain to commit."
options.feedback: Unhelpful to a board that must decide.

lesson: Strategy under uncertainty needs scenarios, not forecasts: find no-regret moves, stage the bets with signposts, and set appetite with the strategy.
